proofUses.reason: The strip cut argument excludes dangling components; the dual Fourier integral has at most ten factors left on the new face after two boundary-edge deletions.
Extract one long edge from each outer route and retain at least N-2 small connector factors in the remaining diagram.
Choose a reachable even moment at fixed dimension, obtain a pointwise coefficient exponent above d+2, then apply the signed Gaussian theorem and convolution transfer.
For d>30 a real K lies between (d+2)/4 and (d-6)/3; the resulting spatial power gives the coefficient tail and fourth moment needed for the signed Gaussian and convolution theorems.
At most two outer edges and one shared edge survive the erased faces, so there are at most three bridges. Lq for q>=6 suffices, and q=9 gives the long-edge coefficient bound.
For d>18 choose (d+2)/4<K<7d/18-2; moment gain and the long-edge bound give the coefficient tail required for the signed Gaussian expansion. Ninth-norm connector smallness remains explicit.
Apply the two-root bound at its sixth-norm endpoint, retain the exact remaining-edge counts, and handle orders zero and one separately.

For d>14 choose (d+2)/2<a<d-6. Moment gain supplies the initial spatial bound; sixth norms double the coefficient exponent past d+2. The signed Green theorem gives the improved remainder, and a second pointwise gain gives moments and continuity below d-4.
